transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it, so day-to-day it feels covered.  

When she steps away—lunch, bathroom, out sick, or after hours—what typically happens to those calls?
User: She tries to call them back when she returns. We don’t really track any missed calls.
Agent: Makes sense, a lot of places handle it that way.  

When she calls back, do you feel most of those people still pick up and book, or do you suspect some of them have already gone with someone else by then?
User: We haven't really counted misses, but I think some might go elsewhere by the time we get back.
Agent: Yeah, that’s usually where the hidden money leaks out.  

If you think about a normal week, when are you and your front-desk girl most likely to miss calls—busy peak hours, lunch, or more after you close?
User: Probably during busy peak hours, but we usually manage to call people back when things settle down.
Agent: Totally hear you — and it’s great she’s on top of callbacks.  

If it turned out you were losing even 2–3 good new customers a week from people not picking up on the callback, would that be meaningful to you, or would that feel pretty minor in your world?
User: I suppose losing new customers isn't ideal, but I'm not convinced it's that significant for us.
Agent: Totally fair, you don’t want to fix something that isn’t really a problem.  

Out of curiosity, what kind of business are you running—so I can put some real numbers to what “a couple lost customers” would actually mean for you?
User: We're an auto body shop. Average ticket is about $1,100 if that helps put things in perspective.
Agent: That helps a lot, thanks — so even a “couple” of missed new customers a week is like $2–3K walking out the door.  

If there were a way for every single call during those peak hours to be answered live and booked on the spot — without hiring another person — would that be worth exploring, or are you really trying to keep things exactly as they are right now?
User: Alright, as a backup layer, I can see it. Book your demo.
Agent: Got it, that makes sense — using it as a backup so you’re not losing those peak-hour callers.  

What day usually works better for you for a quick demo with Jay, earlier in the week or closer to the end of the week?
User: Let's go with earlier in the week for the demo. Tuesday or Wednesday works best.
Agent: Nice, that makes it easy.  

Are mornings or afternoons better for you on those days?
User: Mornings are usually better for me, say around 10 AM.
Agent: Perfect, mornings around 10 work well.  

Which day is better for you this week at 10 AM — Tuesday or Wednesday?
User: Wednesday at 10 AM works best for me. Let's go with that.
Agent: Got it, Wednesday at 10 AM it is — we’ll use that time for a quick walkthrough with Jay focused on catching those peak-hour missed calls for the shop.  

Before I lock that in, what’s the best email to send the calendar invite and a quick summary to?
User: Send it over to dave@kowalskiautobody.com. Looking forward to seeing how this might help us out.
Agent: Perfect, I’ll have the invite and details sent to dave@kowalskiautobody.com for Wednesday at 10, and you’ll also get a text reminder so you can reschedule easily if anything comes up. Jay will walk you through exactly how we can act as that backup layer for peak-hour calls and show real numbers for an auto body shop like yours.

Anything else you want me to note for Jay before that call?
